text:
jess: Hey team — new user trying quickstart Docker sample and hitting an auth/retry loop behind our corporate SSL proxy. first call returns a TLS verify error, then sdk retries and eventually we get 503 from the gateway.

jess: Repro steps they gave:
```
# on Windows w/ Docker Desktop
docker run --rm -e REDWOOD_API_KEY=pk_live_xxx redwood/quickstart:latest node index.js
```
And output:
```
Error: request to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/complete failed, reason: certificate has expired (SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED)
...SDK retrying (attempt 2)...
HTTP 503 Service Unavailable
```

ow onboard-bot: @jess I see the workspace (acme-team) is in trial and billing not fully set up, but that shouldn't cause TLS failures. :thinking_face:

ow owen: Likely the corporate proxy is doing TLS interception (adding its CA). Docker container doesn't trust the corporate CA by default. Two options: mount CA into container or disable proxy for quickstart.

sam: Can we get a clearer error from the SDK? If auth header is being stripped/rewritten, you might see 401 or 403 instead of TLS failure. Any chance of the proxy rewriting headers?

jess: No 401/403 in logs — initial connection fails with CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED. But after retries we do see 503 from our gateway (maybe because the container's retries overwhelm a fallback path).

ow infra-bot: FYI there's a known issue when DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 + company-proxy + node:latest where node's TLS store is not populated with host CA. Tracking: INFRA-3621.

ow owen: Quick suggestions to unblock user:
- Try `docker run --rm -v /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt:/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt:ro ...` if host has CA bundle.
- Or set `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/path/to/corp_ca.pem` in container env.
- For quicker DX, ask them to run the quickstart on host (not in container) to confirm if proxy is the culprit.

jess: They tried host (Windows) first and saw same TLS error from Node. This is a corporate-managed machine so mounting CA is non-trivial.

sam: Two product notes: (1) Quickstart docs should include a troubleshooting section for TLS-proxy environments with the exact env vars and docker volume examples. (2) SDK could detect CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED and produce a friendlier message: "TLS handshake failed — common cause: corporate SSL proxy. See https://go.redwood.ai/quickstart-proxy for remediation".

jess: Agreed. Also the user was confused because onboarding-bot says workspace not fully activated (billing). They thought that was blocking the call. So we should clarify UX: billing gating blocks model selection and long-lived tokens but does not cause TLS handshake failures — different root cause.

ow onboard-bot: Note added to workspace acme-team: "investigate TLS proxy guidance and clarify billing vs network errors".

ow owen: I'll open a small PR to extend quickstart README with a "Behind corporate proxies" troubleshooting blurb + example `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` and a short Docker volume snippet.

jess: Thanks. For this thread: can we provide the user a temporary workaround? If they can run `curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health` from their machine and paste output we can confirm handshake path.

jess: They ran curl and got:
```
* TLSv1.2 (INTERNAL), Cipher is ...
* CAfile: none
* Server certificate: ... issuer=Corp-Intercept-CA
* SSL: certificate verify failed
```

sam: Confirms interception. I'll draft quick message for support: instruct to add corp CA to `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` or use `--network=host` on Linux. If they can't modify machine, suggest temporary use of personal machine or cloud devbox to finish onboarding.

jess: Filing support case and linking back here. Propose we add an actionable SDK error and a line in onboarding flow that says: "Network errors like TLS verify failures are usually local proxy issues — see troubleshooting" so users don't conflate with billing. :white_check_mark:

now infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-3621 and DOCS-784.

jess: Closing loop with user after we publish doc blurb. Thanks all :heart:
